title: SLO-guided Failover Suppressor and Telemetry‑led Runbooks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create an automated suppression layer and telemetry-driven on-call runbooks that use SLO state and regional health signals to control paging, trigger progressive multi-region failover, and apply circuit-breaker based load shedding. This reduces noisy pages while keeping high-fidelity operator visibility and safe escalation paths.

Scope:
- Implement an SLO state service (read-only cache) that collates per-route latency/error budget burn across regions and model variants.
- Build an alert-suppression policy engine that: 1) dynamically suppresses low-signal pages when SLOs are not threatened, 2) escalates immediately when burn-rate crosses configured thresholds, and 3) emits audit events for suppressed pages.
- Integrate suppression decisions with multi-region failover orchestrator: gradual traffic evacuation, circuit-breakers per region/model, and route-level load shedding based on customer tier.
- Author telemetry-led runbook templates (canary checks, rollback criteria, mitigation knobs) with automated remediation steps for common failure classes (GPU OOMs, kernel stalls, KV cache corruption, network partition).
- Add pacing and hysteresis to avoid oscillation: backoff windows, cooldown intervals, and decay curves for suppression.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Aggressive suppression reduces on-call fatigue but risks hiding early indicators; we mitigate with synthetic canaries and a small always-page-critical-signal whitelist.
- Automation will attempt safe remediation first (restart worker, flush KV cache) and fall back to human escalation for multi-region degradations.
- Auditability is critical: every suppressed page will produce an event with runbook link and reasoning stored in the incident timeline.

Success metrics:
- Reduce P1/P2 noisy pages by 40% within first quarter after rollout.
- Decrease mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for true degradations by 30% via more accurate signals and automated mitigations.
- Demonstrate safe regional evacuation in staged canary (zero customer-facing errors for top-10 routes) during the pilot.

Deliverables:
- SLO state cache + public read-only API for alerting engine.
- Suppression policy engine with config UI/console hooks.
- Telemetry-driven runbook library and automation scripts (Terraform/K8s job runbooks + ops tool commands).
- Integration tests and a staged canary plan for multi-region failover.

Risks & mitigation:
- Over-suppression: enforce small set of always-page signals and periodic suppression audits.
- Automation regression: gate runbook automation behind feature flags and require two engineer approvals for production enablement.
- Circuit breaker mis-tuning: start conservative, run synthetic-heavy load tests, and expose tuning knobs in console.
